extracted.intended_audience: researchers (faculty and students), interdisciplinary collaborators, and potential partners interested in the Rotman Institute's programs and priorities
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Rotman Institute's research goals, priorities, supported project types, and activities that guide which research the institute fosters and supports. Useful for researchers seeking alignment with institute themes or applying for institute programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of humanities scholarship into interdisciplinary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrates core humanities scholarship — especially philosophy — into interdisciplinary research in the sciences, social sciences, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institute 'unites scholars across disciplines locally and globally' to address major scientific, technological, and societal challenges; projects should connect philosophical/humanities perspectives with other fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on deep and wicked problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Address major scientific, technological, and societal challenges shaped by what we consider to be deep and wicked problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are expected to target complex, high-stakes problems characterized as 'deep and wicked'; the site repeatedly emphasizes this framing as central to research selection and activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster success for institute researchers at all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: To foster success for institute researchers at all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional goal implies support across career stages (students, postdocs, faculty) through programs and resources that increase researcher success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a research environment that fosters innovative solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a research environment that fosters innovative solutions to deep and wicked problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on cultivating an environment — organizational culture, events, supports — that enables innovation rather than just individual projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide distinctive interdisciplinary training for students
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide distinctive interdisciplinary training for students in the sciences and humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is a stated priority; student-focused programming should combine disciplines (sciences + humanities) and be distinctive compared with standard disciplinary programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate philosophical and ethical considerations into science, technology, and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To integrate philosophical and ethical considerations into science, technology, and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and activities should explicitly incorporate philosophical and ethical analysis relevant to scientific and policy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform and engage the public on deep and wicked problems
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform and engage the public on deep and wicked problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public engagement and communication are part of the institute's mission; work should include or enable outreach, public-facing outputs, or engagement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical research priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Priorities: Knowledge in the 21st Century; Societal Impact of Emerging Technologies; Challenges in Public Health; Foundations of Physics, Neuroscience, and the Mind; Think Tank Projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These named themes indicate topical areas the institute prioritizes; proposals and projects aligned with these topics are more directly relevant to the institute's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think Tank project criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Think Tank projects address deep and wicked challenges; foster collaboration across disciplines and sectors; develop innovative research programs; and position teams for major external funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think Tank projects are supported by the Interdisciplinary Think Tank Program and are expected to be cross-sectoral, collaborative, program-building, and oriented toward scalability and funding-readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute-supported project support model
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute Supported Projects encompass a wide range of interdisciplinary initiatives at various stages of development; the institute provides strategic, organizational, and collaborative support to help research teams refine ideas, build partnerships, and advance research agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is not limited to mature projects; teams at different development stages can receive strategic/organizational/collaborative help aimed at idea refinement, partnership-building, and agenda advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research activities and collaborative fora
rubrics_metrics.description: The institute supports various research activities, including reading groups, working groups, and research meetings and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are intended to bring together scholars and partners from diverse disciplines and sectors to explore shared questions, exchange ideas, and develop collaborative research projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty expertise and thematic networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty members bring research expertise across areas (e.g., Artificial Intelligence and Computation; Ecological Philosophy; Emerging Technologies and Social Impact; Environment and Climate Change; Ethics; Governance and Public Policy; History and Philosophy of Science; Philosophy of Mind and Neuroscience; Philosophy of Physics and Experimental Physics; Public Health and Health Policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Faculty Member Network Map highlights thematic expertise and connections; prospective collaborators should consider how their work connects to these areas and to existing member networks for interdisciplinary collaboration.
